hero.title: Inflation, gas and tariffs in 2026: the claims against the data.
hero.lede: The administration says inflation is low, gas is cheaper than under Biden, the pump spike is the Iran war and tariffs don't raise prices. Economists, journalists and the Fed say otherwise, or something more complicated. This page pulls the testable claims out of those videos and checks each one against BLS, EIA and Federal Reserve data.

recap.bottomLine: the measurable parts of the administration's account mostly fail for autumn 2026 and mostly held a year earlier. BLS data put September 2026 inflation above every 2024 and 2025 reading, so "low by historical standards" is wrong now and was right in January; "no inflation" is wrong in every period. Gasoline really was cheaper than the Biden-era average through February 2026, then the Iran war pushed it a quarter above that average, below only the 2022 peak. The New York Fed's tariff study finds US buyers bear nearly all of the tariff and about a quarter reaches shelf prices, so "tariffs don't raise prices" is wrong, though the tariff push to goods inflation peaked in February 2026 and is fading while the price level stays higher. The war raising gas prices is right; prices falling back when it ends is a prediction the data cannot yet judge. Real wages fell over the year to September 2026. {hypeWrong} of {hypeTotal} sweeping claims ("no inflation", "tariffs cause wealth", "prices are falling") are judged wrong; "booming" gets a partly, since GDP is growing at trend while real wages fall.
